title: Close the device-credential authenticate timing side channel

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0074 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive 'dale al merge y a lo que sigue' — the eighth hardening fix, closing the device-credential authenticate timing side channel. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0074.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: The hardening audit found DeviceCredentialLifecycle.authenticate returns null immediately when the credential record is absent, before running the sealed-verifier comparison, so an attacker can distinguish an existing credentialId (slower, the comparison runs) from an unknown one (fast) by timing, revealing which credentialIds exist.
claims.evidence: protocol/src/device-credential.ts authenticate prior early return; the 2026-08-24 hardening-audit finding hardening-authenticate-credential-timing.

claims.statement: The change always runs the secretCodec.matches comparison — against a fixed dummy verifier of representative length (okdv1$sha256$ plus 43 characters) when the credential is absent or its stored verifier is malformed — and then returns null unless a usable record actually matched. The store lookup no longer creates a fast path.
claims.evidence: protocol/src/device-credential.ts DUMMY_SEALED_SECRET and the rewritten authenticate.

claims.statement: Governed discovery equalized the verifier-comparison branch, which dominates the cost, rather than attempting full constant-time token parsing, because the finding is specifically about credentialId existence — which the store-lookup-then-compare asymmetry revealed.
claims.evidence: The comparison (a hash plus a constant-time equal) is the expensive step; the store lookup returns present/absent quickly either way.

claims.statement: Proving with a spy codec that matches() is invoked exactly once for both an absent and a present credential, while the absent case returns null and the present authenticates, closes the timing side channel.

The dummy verifier is a fixed, non-matching value; the fix removes the store-lookup timing asymmetry but does not make the whole authenticate path constant-time — a malformed or non-prefixed token still returns early, which reveals malformedness rather than credentialId existence.
claims.evidence: protocol/src/device-credential.ts parseToken early return precedes the store lookup.

claims.statement: The change is in the protocol package (device-credential.ts) plus its test; the server consumes the rebuilt protocol dist. No server-source or Studio change, and the server device-credential auth path is behaviorally unchanged for valid tokens.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0074 branch: protocol/src/device-credential.ts and protocol/tests/device-credential.test.ts; the full server suite passes unchanged.

successCriteria.statement: The verifier comparison runs for an absent credential, not only a present one.
successCriteria.verification: A spy-codec test asserts matches() is invoked exactly once when authenticating a well-formed token for a non-existent credentialId, and the call returns null.

successCriteria.statement: A present credential still authenticates with the same single comparison.
successCriteria.verification: The same test asserts a real token invokes matches() once and returns an authority.
The protocol suite and the full server suite pass; the server device-credential HTTP lifecycle is unchanged.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0074 records the timing-oracle finding and its constant-work fix before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: authenticate always runs the verifier comparison against the real or a fixed dummy verifier before deciding.
A test proves the comparison runs for absent and present credentials; the protocol and server suites pass.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
